Question: A total of \(28\) handshakes was exchanged at the conclusion of a party. Assuming that each participant was equally polite toward all the others, the number of people present was:
Solution:
Use the usual convention that every pair of people exchanges exactly one handshake. Let \(n\) be the number of people. Each person shakes hands with the other \(n-1\) people, so the total number of individual participations in handshakes is \(n(n-1)\).

Every handshake contributes exactly two participations, one for each person involved. Thus every handshake is included, with the same multiplicity of two, and
\[
n(n-1)=2\cdot28=56.
\]
Since \(8\cdot7=56\), we get \(n=8\). The product \(n(n-1)\) strictly increases for integers \(n\ge2\), so no other party size gives this total. There were \(\boxed{8}\) people, choice \(\boxed{\text{D}}\).
